entities.description: Acting/only physician after Roeder's death; investigator.
Dead senior physician; serum experimenter; found in locked room.
The matron; keeps keys, morphine, registers; burned the Cordier chart.
False-name patient in room 14 (as 'Madame Variel'); Jonas's sister.
Hélène's brother; died 1905 under Roeder's serum; buried above the house.
Young nurse; flagged the ledger discrepancy; fetched the master key.
Asthmatic long-term resident; remembers everything.
18, the second patient; subject of Roeder's renewed serum.
Caretaker; keeps the funicular and its maintenance log; took bribes for silence.
Lawyer in Lyon acting for the Cordier family.
The morphine ledger; doses signed out against patients.
Master key to the consulting room, kept in the matron's cabinet.
Roeder's own key, found on the blotter inside the locked room.
Brown vial of Tinct. Digitalin, two doses short.
Roeder's black diary with a brass lock.
Roeder's unsent resignation, broken off at 'conscience'.
The last telegram before the line cut, addressed to Roeder, marked private.
Earlier Veilloz telegram kept in Roeder's drawer (1905 matter).
Madame Variel's forged admission papers.
Bochat's funicular maintenance log with blank nights.
Marguerite Sève's chart with the abrupt cipher-marked change.
The oldest chart (Jonas Cordier 1905), burned in the stove.
Room fourteen's snow-soaked boots.
Hélène's locket: Jonas's portrait and her true name.
The admission register with the née column.
Belvoir's chapel register of the dead.
Roeder's secret serum/protocol tried on the poor and friendless.
The snowed-in sanatorium, former Grand Hôtel Belvoir.
Roeder's locked consulting room at the quiet end.
Hélène's room in the south wing.
The walled burial ground above the house.
The funicular/cog-rail down to Brassac.
